fields.Participants: Store Manager, Paint Section Lead, DENR-Certified Hazardous Waste Vendor
fields.Trigger: Paint mixing station waste accumulation or quarterly disposal cycle

Automation Opportunity: - Accumulation-date → auto 90-day countdown → auto-trigger vendor pickup work order at day 75; manifest upload → auto-block vendor invoice payment until matched to logged accumulation
Controls: - CTL-449 (ensure controlled execution — Hazardous Waste & DENR Compliance (PA-73.2).)
- operational: DENR-certified vendor onboarding; CTL-44 (duplicate-invoice guard on disposal invoices); operational control: manifest-vs-invoice match before payment
Pain Points / Risks: - **Regulatory risk**: exceeding the DENR 90-day storage limit (DAO 2013-22) triggers fines/permit risk; mitigated by the 90-day countdown alert and quarterly vendor pickup cadence

- **Manifest-integrity risk**: missing/mis-matched manifest forfeits the compliance record and the vendor-cost deduction; mitigated by mandatory manifest capture before vendor payment (operational control)
System Touchpoints: - ERP sustainability / hazwaste sub-ledger — accumulation start-date, volume, category, 90-day-limit countdown alert (links to W2609 DENR permit; W2612 audit)
- Paint mixing/colorant module — colorant/thinner consumption linkage (W168) feeding waste-volume estimate
- Document management — 5-year manifest archive (links to VS-88 records retention; legal-hold capable)
- Financials (AP) — disposal-cost posting per store (PHP 30–50K/qtr × 200 ≈ PHP 24–40M/yr)
Time Estimate: ~15–20 min/store/day accumulation + 15 min/week monitoring + quarterly pickup (~2 hrs/store/qtr) + Finance batch. ~PHP 24–40M/yr network disposal cost.

steps.activity: Paint Section Lead manages daily paint waste: leftover tint, contaminated thinner, paint spills, empty cans with residue; collects in designated hazardous waste containers with proper labeling per DENR requirements

Store Manager monitors hazardous waste accumulation: tracks volume against DENR storage limits (90-day on-site accumulation limit per DAO 2013-22 (the revised RA 6969 Procedural Manual)), ensures containers properly sealed and labeled

DENR-certified hazardous waste vendor conducts quarterly pickup; issues manifest document; Store Manager signs and archives for 5-year compliance record; Finance processes disposal cost (PHP 30–50K/quarter per store)

fields.Participants: Dept Supervisor, Maintenance Staff, Safety Officer, DENR-Certified Vendor
fields.Trigger: Solvent waste from paint station or equipment cleaning

Automation Opportunity: - Monthly Safety inspection checklist on mobile with photo evidence → auto-file to Fire Code compliance record; manifest auto-linked to disposal cost
Controls: - CTL-06 (vendor certification); operational control: monthly Safety Officer cabinet inspection with signed checklist; BFP FSIC linkage (W476)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fire risk**: flammable solvent waste in unapproved containers or near ignition sources → BFP Fire Code violation and fire risk; mitigated by approved-cabinet requirement + monthly Safety inspection
- **Cradle-to-grave risk**: gap in manifest chain ⇒ RA 6969 liability if waste is mishandled downstream; mitigated by cradle-to-grave ledger and DENR-certified vendor (CTL-06)
System Touchpoints: - ERP sustainability module — solvent-waste cradle-to-grave ledger with manifest reference (links to VS-114 DG/hazmat; VS-24.3 fixed-site hazmat storage)
- Flammable-storage / Fire Code module — BFP Fire Code compliance records, cabinet inspection log (links to W476 FSIC)
- HSE module — monthly Safety Officer inspection record (links to VS-24 HSE; W141 safety inspection)
Time Estimate: ~10–15 min/store/day segregation + 30 min/month inspection + monthly/quarterly collection. Network: ~200 stores × daily = absorbed into paint-station routine.

steps.activity: Department Supervisor segregates solvent waste: used thinner, mineral spirits, acetone; stores in approved flammable liquid containers in flammable storage cabinet
Safety Officer inspects flammable storage monthly: verifies container integrity, ventilation, fire suppression, signage, PPE availability
DENR-certified vendor collects flammable waste per schedule; issues transport manifest; waste tracked cradle to grave in ERP sustainability module

fields.Participants: DC Ops / Store Manager, DENR-Certified Lead Recycler, Safety Officer
fields.Trigger: Forklift battery replacement or customer battery return

Automation Opportunity: - Forklift battery asset retirement → auto-trigger certified-recycler work order; auto-recover lead credit against asset NBV
Controls: - CTL-449 (ensure controlled execution — Hazardous Waste & DENR Compliance (PA-73.2).)
- operational: certified recycler onboarding; CTL-26 (asset disposal); operational control: 100% manifest-traceability review quarterly
Pain Points / Risks: - **Environmental liability**: lead-acid batteries sent to uncertified recycler violate RA 6969 and create soil/groundwater liability; mitigated by 100%-certified-recycler rule (CTL-06) and manifest trail
- **Acid-burn/injury risk**: handling cracked/leaking batteries; mitigated by acid-resistant containment + PPE (VS-24)
System Touchpoints: - ERP sustainability module — battery-waste ledger with DENR manifest + lead-recovery credit (links to W2612 audit; VS-114 DG)
- Fixed-asset / fleet module — forklift battery asset retirement (links to W188 fleet spare parts; CTL-26)
- Financials (AR/misc income) — lead-recovery credit posting (PHP 500–1,500/battery)
Time Estimate: Per-event (~1–2 hrs) × ~3–5/store/yr × ~~205 locations ≈ ~600–1,000 events/yr network; quarterly review ~1 day.

steps.activity: DC Ops / Store Manager manages spent lead-acid batteries: stores upright in acid-resistant containment, labels as hazardous waste, contacts certified lead recycler
Lead recycler collects batteries: weighs and issues receipt with DENR manifest; pays lead recovery credit (PHP 500–1,500 per battery)
Sustainability Coordinator tracks battery waste: ensures 100% go to certified recyclers per RA 6969 (Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act)

workflows.name: DENR Hazardous Waste Permit & Registration Management

Automation Opportunity: - Permit-expiry → 90/60/30-day auto-alert → auto-generate renewal work order with pre-filled prior-year submission; permit-status block on new-location hazwaste generation if lapsed
Controls: - CTL-41: permit-compliance alerting — directly applies; operational control: Legal completeness review before submission
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lapse risk**: expired DENR registration ⇒ illegal hazardous-waste generation status, fines, operational risk; mitigated by 60-day expiry alert (CTL-41) and renewal-cycle tracking
- **Multi-location inconsistency risk**: 205 locations across DENR-EMB regions with varying requirements; mitigated by central permit ledger and Legal pre-review
System Touchpoints: - Regulatory/permit module — DENR ECC + HW Generator Registration per location with expiry countdown (links to VS-22 regulatory permits; CTL-41 permit-compliance control)
- Location master (W254) — permit status per location; links to VS-76 multi-LGU compliance
- Document management — permit archive (VS-88 records retention; legal-hold capable)
Time Estimate: ~1–2 months/location-cycle prep (spread across 205 locations, batched by region) + ongoing archive. Central Coordinator effort ~2–3 FTE-days/month steady-state.

steps.activity: Sustainability Coordinator maintains DENR Environmental Compliance Certificate and Hazardous Waste Generator Registration for all 205 locations; tracks renewal deadlines; compiles required documentation
Legal reviews submissions for completeness; ensures compliance with DENR DAO 2013-22 and RA 6969; Coordinator submits to DENR-EMB regional office
Coordinator archives all DENR permits and correspondence in document management system; maintains 5-year rolling compliance record per location

fields.Frequency: Monthly for store lighting; quarterly customer events
fields.Participants: Maintenance Staff, Store Manager, DENR-Certified Vendor
fields.Trigger: Lighting replacement cycle or customer collection event

Automation Opportunity: - Lighting-asset replacement log → auto-generate mercury-waste accumulation entry; loyalty auto-issue points at customer drop-off
Controls: - CTL-449 (ensure controlled execution — Hazardous Waste & DENR Compliance (PA-73.2).)
- operational: certified vendor; operational control: dedicated-container + no-general-stream rule audited in W2612
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mercury-release risk**: broken CFL/tube releases mercury vapor — health + environmental hazard; mitigated by dedicated unbreakable collection containers and breakage-response procedure
- **Contamination risk**: mercury waste entering general stream ⇒ RA 6969 violation; mitigated by separate stream + manifest
System Touchpoints: - ERP sustainability module — mercury-waste volume + manifest (links to W2612 audit; RA 6969)
- Loyalty module — bonus-points for customer drop-off (links to VS-13)
- Facility/lighting asset module — lighting replacement cycle (links to VS-20.3 facility maintenance)
Time Estimate: Per-replacement (~10 min) absorbed into facility routine + quarterly customer event (~1 day/store) + per-collection manifest. Network ~200 stores.

steps.activity: Maintenance Staff replaces burnt-out CFL bulbs and fluorescent tubes; carefully handles to prevent breakage; stores spent bulbs in dedicated CFL collection containers
Store Manager hosts quarterly customer CFL/bulb collection: accepts household CFLs, fluorescent tubes; partners with DENR-certified recycler; offers loyalty points
DENR-certified vendor collects mercury-containing waste: issues manifest; Coordinator tracks volume and ensures no mercury waste enters general waste stream

fields.Frequency: Ad-hoc; 2–5 spills per year across network
fields.Participants: Safety Officer, Store/DC Manager, Maintenance Staff, DENR (if significant)
fields.Trigger: Chemical spill at store or DC

Automation Opportunity: - Mobile spill-report app with severity-decision tree → auto-escalate to DENR reportable threshold → auto-notify Insurance/VP; spill-kit inventory auto-decrement
Controls: - CTL-449 (ensure controlled execution — Hazardous Waste & DENR Compliance (PA-73.2).)
- Operational control: spill-kit inventory check in monthly Safety inspection; incident-report dual-signoff (Safety Officer + Store Manager); insurance evidence within 48 hrs
Pain Points / Risks: - **Escalation risk**: minor spill mis-classified and not escalated ⇒ environmental contamination + DENR reporting failure; mitigated by severity-decision tree (5-liter/hazardous threshold) and Safety Officer authority to escalate
- **Drain-entry risk**: spill reaching storm drain ⇒ serious environmental incident; mitigated by drain-protection in spill kits and containment-first response
System Touchpoints: - HSE/incident module — spill incident record with severity, photos, root cause, corrective action (links to VS-24 HSE W140 OHS incident management; VS-114 DG spill)
- ERP sustainability module — environmental-contamination reporting to DENR-EMB if significant (RA 6969; links to W433 DENR SMR/CMR)
- Insurance/claims module — damage claim if applicable (links to VS-26 insurance)
Time Estimate: Immediate response (minutes) + 15–60 min assessment + 1–2 days documentation. ~2–5 events/yr network but each carries high severity tail-risk.

steps.activity: First responder activates spill response: dons PPE from spill kit, identifies spilled material, contains spill using absorbent materials, prevents entry into drains

Safety Officer assesses spill severity: minor (<5 liters) — staff cleans; major (>5 liters or hazardous) — evacuates area, calls emergency contractor, reports to DENR if environmental contamination possible
Safety Officer documents spill: incident report with photos, root cause analysis, corrective actions; updates spill kit inventory; submits to COO and Insurance if damage occurred

fields.Trigger: Internal audit cycle or DENR inspection

workflows.name: Hazardous Waste Compliance Audit & Record Keeping

Automation Opportunity: - DENR-inspection "readiness dashboard" — real-time completeness check of manifests/certs/training per location, with red flags for any gap
Controls: - CTL-449 (ensure controlled execution — Hazardous Waste & DENR Compliance (PA-73.2).)
- operational: annual internal audit sampling 20–30 locations; CAPA tracking per W333
Pain Points / Risks: - **Inspection-readiness risk**: DENR ad-hoc inspection finds incomplete manifests ⇒ fines/permit risk; mitigated by inspection-ready 5-year archive and annual internal audit
- **Finding-drift risk**: audit findings not remediated within SLA; mitigated by 30/7-day CAPA tracking (W333)
System Touchpoints: - Internal audit module — hazwaste compliance audit program + findings/CAPA tracking (links to VS-21 internal audit W339 regulatory compliance audit; W333 CAPA)
- Document management — 5-year hazwaste record retention per location (links to VS-88; legal-hold capable; DENR-inspection-ready)
- ERP sustainability module — source generation logs and manifests under audit
Time Estimate: ~2–3 weeks/year internal audit + finding remediation (30-day SLA) + ongoing archive maintenance. ~20–30 locations sampled/yr.

steps.activity: Internal Auditor reviews hazardous waste compliance at sampled locations (20–30/year): verifies storage compliance, reviews disposal manifests, confirms vendor DENR certification, checks training records
Sustainability Coordinator addresses findings: corrects non-compliance within 30 days; critical findings corrected within 7 days

Coordinator maintains 5-year hazardous waste records per location: generation logs, disposal manifests, vendor certifications, inspection reports, training records; accessible for DENR inspection at any time

fields.Participants: Facilities Mgr, Licensed Contractor, DENR, Safety Officer

Automation Opportunity: - PMO stage-gate block: remodel project cannot pass "demolition" gate without completed asbestos survey + DENR permit (if found) attached
Controls: - CTL-449 (ensure controlled execution — Hazardous Waste & DENR Compliance (PA-73.2).)
- operational: DENR-licensed contractor onboarding; operational control: Safety Officer containment monitoring; permanent manifest archive
Pain Points / Risks: - **Health-liability risk**: unlicensed removal or fiber release exposes workers/customers to asbestos ⇒ severe health + legal liability; mitigated by DENR-licensed-contractor requirement + containment + survey-before-renovation gate
- **Discovery-late risk**: asbestos found mid-renovation ⇒ project stop-work and cost/schedule overrun; mitigated by mandatory pre-renovation survey
System Touchpoints: - Capex/project module — asbestos survey as a mandatory remodel gate (links to VS-109 store remodel; VS-112 PMO stage-gate; VS-40 capex)
- HSE module — containment/PPE compliance monitoring (links to VS-24; VS-114 DG)
- Document management — permanent asbestos-disposal archive (links to VS-88; legal-hold)
Time Estimate: ~2–4 weeks pre-renovation survey + per-project removal (days-weeks) + documentation. ~10–15 projects/yr, low frequency but high-severity tail.

steps.activity: Facilities Manager conducts asbestos survey before renovation; if found: engages DENR-licensed removal contractor; obtains DENR permit
Licensed contractor performs removal with full PPE and containment; Safety Officer monitors compliance
Contractor transports to DENR-licensed asbestos landfill; issues disposal manifest; Facilities Manager archives documentation permanently
